Candid

/KAN-did/ — rhymes with sandal · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is candid speaks honestly and directly, even about things that might be uncomfortable to admit.

Her candid review admitted the play's first act was dull.

Worked Example

During the parent-teacher meeting, the teacher gave a candid assessment of the student's work, pointing out exactly where he struggled without softening the critique.

Candid is more precise than 'honest' because it emphasizes speaking directly about uncomfortable truths. The teacher wasn't just being truthful; she was directly addressing difficult shortcomings in a way that cannot be avoided, which is exactly what candid means.

How Candid Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

honest

honest: truthful and sincere in what you say

frank

frank: direct and plain-spoken, holding nothing back

straightforward

straightforward: clear and direct, without evasion or complication

Antonyms

evasive

evasive: dodging direct answers to hide the truth

guarded

guarded: careful and reluctant to reveal one's thoughts

How Strong Is It? — diplomatic → honest → frank → candid

diplomatic vs. candid

diplomatic vs. candid: Diplomatic is the gentlest word on this scale — a diplomatic speaker cushions the truth to spare feelings, while a candid one states it openly, even when it stings.

honest vs. candid

honest vs. candid: Honest means truthful, but candid goes further: an honest person won't tell a lie, while a candid person volunteers uncomfortable truths directly.

frank vs. candid

frank vs. candid: Frank is very close to candid — both mean plain-spoken — but candid is the strongest, suggesting complete openness even about things most people would rather hide.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cand

Root — cand: to shine, glow white (Latin (candere))

Suffix — -id

Suffix — -id: having the quality of (adjective-forming) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Cand- means 'to shine or glow white' and -id forms adjectives, so candid originally meant 'shining white, pure.' A candid person's words have that same bright, unstained quality — nothing shadowy or hidden in what they say.

Use the root in a new word: candidate

Use the root in a new word: candidate: In ancient Rome, a candidate for office wore a gleaming white toga — the same shining-white root that gives candid its sense of pure, open honesty.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Candid is a more formal, serious word than 'honest.' Use candid when someone is speaking difficult truths directly, even though it's uncomfortable. For everyday truthfulness, 'honest' is simpler and more natural.
